me-nuc-natanz.n: Natanz Fuel Enrichment Plant (FEP) and Pilot FEP (PFEP)
me-nuc-natanz.st: struck 2025 and 2026; no IAEA access since June 2025
me-nuc-natanz.what: Israel’s military attacks on Iran’s nuclear facilities began on 13 Jun 2025, and the United States attacked three facilities, including Natanz, on 22 Jun 2025 (IAEA GOV/2026/50; DoD briefing, 22 Jun 2025). Reported: the IAEA Director General said on 16 Jun 2025 that the above-ground Pilot Fuel Enrichment Plant and the site’s power infrastructure had been destroyed (statement read only via a search summary). 3 Mar 2026: IAEA satellite analysis showed damage to the entrance buildings of the Fuel Enrichment Plant, and Iran reported further attacks on 12 and 21 Mar 2026 (GOV/2026/33). The FEP and PFEP are among seven declared facilities the IAEA assesses were affected by the June 2025 attacks and had held nuclear material (GOV/2026/50).

me-nuc-fordow.st: struck 22 Jun 2025; no IAEA access since
me-nuc-fordow.what: 22 Jun 2025: U.S. strike, which the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs called Operation Midnight Hammer. DoD said B-2 bombers dropped a total of 14 GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrators on two nuclear target areas, starting at Fordow; on 26 Jun 2025 DoD described one weapon removing each targeted ventilation-shaft cap and five more following it down. Reported: the IAEA Director General said craters were visible but underground damage could not be assessed (22 Jun 2025, statement page could not be opened at this check). The FFEP is among the facilities the IAEA lists as affected by the June 2025 attacks and had held nuclear material (GOV/2026/50).

me-nuc-isfahan.n: Isfahan nuclear site (UCF, FMP, FPFP, EUPP, IFEP; tunnel complex)
me-nuc-isfahan.ty: uranium conversion, fuel fabrication, enriched-UF6 storage tunnels
me-nuc-isfahan.st: struck 2025; no IAEA access since June 2025
me-nuc-isfahan.what: Israel’s attacks began on 13 Jun 2025 (GOV/2026/50). 22 Jun 2025: a U.S. submarine launched more than two dozen Tomahawk land-attack cruise missiles at surface infrastructure at Isfahan (DoD). Reported: the IAEA Director General said conversion buildings were hit and that entrances to tunnels used to store enriched material appeared to have been hit (22 Jun 2025, statement page could not be opened at this check). The tunnel complex had stored UF6 enriched up to 20% and 60% U-235 (GOV/2026/33). Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched up to 60% by the time of the June 2025 attacks, and the IAEA has not been able to verify it since (GOV/2026/33). Iran says the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP) was also attacked; the IAEA does not know its precise whereabouts.

Iran reported that the plant was attacked on 27 Mar 2026, and IAEA satellite analysis on 29 Mar 2026 showed it had “sustained severe damage” (GOV/2026/33). src.t: IAEA Radiological Assessment Reports Series, 'Radiological Conditions in Areas of Kuwait with Residues of Depleted Uranium' (STI/PUB/1164, 2003)
